reason: As written the falsifier does not discriminate. (1) Ill-posed arms: s(P)=phi_{i(P)}(P) lands in l+1 different codomain curves E_i; 2-sums across codomains are undefined, so 'coverage of s(B)+s(B)' is only defined per codomain. Since #E=r is prime and l!=r, each phi_i is a bijection on F_p-points (kernel order l, |kappa|^{m-1}=1), so decompositions of phi_i(R) by phi_i(B_i) are in exact bijection with decompositions of R by B_i subset of B. Piecewise transport conservation therefore applies on every piece: the outcome is forced (ratio <=1, about 1/(l+1) per-codomain if base size is matched in total) and is a theorem, not a statistic. Prediction_if_true (>1.2 and growing) is unreachable: coverage <= |S|^2/2 for any set S and a random S already nearly attains that when |S|^2<<r. Prediction_if_false (1.00+-0.03) would also likely be violated by the partition penalty, so a FALSE run would not even match the stated falsifier outcome. (2) Wrong metric and regime: B=p^{1/2} gives |S|^2/r ~ 1/4..1, the saturation/ceiling regime, where coverage ratio is bounded by a constant and cannot 'grow with p'; yield mean is the summation-cover double count (closed). The CGK quantity that matters (oracle cost D per membership test, B*D^2 vs N) is not measured: s(B) loses the free x<B membership test (needs l+1 preimage/isogeny evaluations), so the equal-size random control (no membership cost either, in the opposite direction) is not the matched null. (3) Scaling to n=131: nothing transfers; toy sits at B~sqrt(r) while the programme question lives at B<<sqrt(r); no scaling variable (log-log slope in p of a counted-ops quantity) is fitted, only 5 octaves with 20 curves. (4) Runnable: yes with gp only (elldivpol/factormod to detect l+1 rational subgroups, ellisogeny with kernel polynomial, 2^14..2^18, B<=512 points => seconds of CPU per curve). Caveat: prime-order curves with Frobenius scalar mod l (all l+1 subgroups rational) are rare, roughly 1/(24 ln p) for l=3 and 1/(120 ln p) for l=5 per random (a,b); random search is slow (a 20-curve-per-p random-scan gp run exceeded 2 CPU-minutes without output), so use CM-style construction (choose t with t^2-4p = 0 mod l^2, #E=p+1-t prime, then ellfromj on Hilbert-class-polynomial roots mod p or scan j) instead. The work is cheap, which is itself a symptom: the experiment is a unit test of a lemma already in the programme, not an empirical test of an open question.
fix: Replace with two parts, both gp/python3, <=5 CPU-min. PART A (lemma check, exact, not statistical): for each of 20 prime-order E per (p,l) with l+1 rational l-isogenies, p in {2^14,2^16,2^18}, l in {3,5}, build phi_i via ellisogeny (kernel poly from elldivpol factors). Partition B={P: x(P)<Bx} by a coordinate rule i(P)=x mod (l+1) (and a random-label null i(P)=random). For every R in a sample of 10^4 targets, assert #ordered 2-decomps of phi_i(R) in E_i by phi_i(B_i) == #ordered 2-decomps of R by B_i (expect 100% exact equality, 0 violations). A single violation falsifies the 'piecewise transport' reading; 0 violations closes the idea as accounting with the piecewise-bijection argument as the named obstruction (scope: any selection rule, since each piece is homomorphic and sums are intra-piece). PART B (the version that can still be non-trivial): pulled-back multi-curve base S = union_i phi_i^{-1}({Q in E_i : x(Q)<Bx}) subset E, i.e. the 'small-x on every isogenous model' base. Arms: (a) S, (b) single-curve base {x<(l+1)*Bx} on E of equal total size, (c) random subset of E of equal size, (d) positive control: S' = B + t*G for random shift (translate; must give coverage ratio 1.00) and a planted-gain control: a base closed under a known order-3 map (or a union of a subgroup coset if one exists on a non-prime-order curve, e.g. 2 | #E) to prove the instrument detects ratio>1.2 additive energy. Use |S| ~ r^{0.40} so |S|^2/(2r) << 1 (no saturation). Metrics, all counted: M1 = |S+S| / (|S|(|S|+1)/2) (sum coverage, expect 1-O(|S|^2/r)); M2 = additive energy E(S)/E(random of same size) (expect 1.00+-0.05; >1.2 would be structure); M3 = counted F_p mults per membership test D (l+1 isogeny evaluations of degree-l maps, ~(l+1)*c*l mults vs 1 comparison) and the certificate ratio (|S|*D^2)/(r) reported against the single-curve base; expect |S|D^2 worse by (l+1)^3. Fit log-log slope of M2 and M3-ratio against log p over 2^14..2^22 (use 8 p values, 20 curves each, bootstrap CI) and state prediction: slope 0+-0.1 means accounting; slope >0.1 with CI excluding 0 survives as lead. Success metric is structural (additive energy, distinct sums, counted mults), never wall time. Scope statement to log: toy result says nothing about n=131 beyond the certificate scaling slope; it can only close or keep open the 'non-homomorphic selection acts as sum-correlated filter' reading (KN-OPEN-91d4f6 flavour), and the Hecke/X_0(l) correspondence itself acts on the j-line, not on E(F_p), so the label 'Hecke correspondence' should be dropped or justified.
